course.title: Next.js — From Beginner to Professional Practice
course.description: A visual-first, project-based Next.js course mapped to the complete 268-topic syllabus in the supplied 54-page PDF. Covers the App Router, legacy Pages Router, full-stack data flow, security, testing, performance, deployment, and professional workflows.
course.version_scope: Next.js 16 documentation snapshot checked 2026-10-18. The official installation guide states Node.js 20.9 minimum. Use JavaScript and JSX for the primary path; TypeScript remains an optional parallel skill. Caching, Proxy, experimental and deployment-specific features must be verified against the exact release and hosting model before use.
prerequisites: basic React, JSX, components, props, and state
course.estimated_workload_note: The PDF estimates 12–20 weeks for the core path plus additional time for Pages Router, advanced specializations, and the capstone. Actual effort depends on prior React experience and practice time.
learning_outcomes: Create Next.js applications and structure routes/layouts.
Choose Server and Client Components deliberately.
Fetch and mutate data with robust loading/error and cache behavior.
Implement secure Route Handlers, authentication, and authorization.
Optimize metadata, assets, accessibility, performance, and production reliability.
Test, deploy, monitor, debug, and maintain App Router and Pages Router applications.

learning_roadmap.title: Orientation and setup
learning_roadmap.goal: Understand the framework, install tools, create a project, and learn file conventions.

learning_roadmap.title: Routing and UI fundamentals
learning_roadmap.goal: Build pages, layouts, navigation, Server and Client Components, and reusable styling.

learning_roadmap.title: Data-driven applications
learning_roadmap.goal: Fetch data, integrate services, understand caching/revalidation, and build resilient loading and error states.

learning_roadmap.title: Full-stack functionality
learning_roadmap.goal: Implement forms, mutations, endpoints, authentication, authorization, and secure data access.

learning_roadmap.title: Discoverability and interaction
learning_roadmap.goal: Add metadata, optimize assets, handle client-side state, and learn advanced routing.

learning_roadmap.title: Advanced framework knowledge
learning_roadmap.goal: Study Proxy, configuration, testing, bundle optimization, performance, and cache diagnosis.

learning_roadmap.title: Professional readiness
learning_roadmap.goal: Improve accessibility, deployment, maintainability, debugging, and production reliability.

learning_roadmap.title: Legacy expertise
learning_roadmap.goal: Learn Pages Router conventions and incremental migration once App Router foundations are secure.

learning_roadmap.title: Applied mastery
learning_roadmap.goal: Complete exercises, projects, and the production-style multi-vendor marketplace capstone.

source_correction_log.source_note: The supplied PDF describes a modern App Router-first curriculum and flags version-sensitive behavior.
source_correction_log.verification: Official Next.js installation documentation checked on 2026-10-18 describes Next.js 16 docs and a minimum Node.js version of 20.9.
source_correction_log.decision: Use Next.js 16 as the documentation snapshot; learners and instructors must verify exact installed version and supported hosting runtime.

source_correction_log.source_note: The PDF teaches Proxy terminology and separates older Middleware details into the legacy module.
source_correction_log.verification: Current official docs say the middleware convention is deprecated and renamed to proxy in Next.js 16.
source_correction_log.decision: Teach proxy.js/proxy() for the Next.js 16 path; preserve middleware material only for older projects and migration context.

source_correction_log.source_note: The PDF warns that Next.js caching behavior differs between releases.
source_correction_log.verification: Official docs describe Cache Components via cacheComponents and `use cache`, with a separate prior caching model.
source_correction_log.decision: Mark cache defaults/configuration as version-sensitive; examples identify the selected model and require version-matched testing.

source_correction_log.source_note: The PDF says TypeScript is useful but not mandatory for a JavaScript learning path.
source_correction_log.verification: This repository task mandates JavaScript/JSX only and forbids adding .ts/.tsx files.
source_correction_log.decision: Use JavaScript/JSX examples and configuration; no .ts or .tsx files are added.

source_correction_log.source_note: The PDF includes screenshots and residual interface text/third-party label artifacts on pages, in addition to the syllabus.
source_correction_log.decision: Extracted lesson titles and subtopics from the parsed pages; original SVG diagrams replace screenshots and unrelated branding. The syllabus topics remain mapped; no external artwork is copied.

source_correction_log.source_note: Section B lists 24 modules and 268 numbered topics; Sections C–G describe 26 exercises, 11 projects, advanced specialist topics, tracks, and checkpoints.
source_correction_log.decision: All 268 lessons, 26 exercises, 11 project briefs, final assessment blueprint, specialist topics, learning tracks, roadmap phases, and coverage notes are represented in separate files.
